newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices ease on new crop arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices ease on new crop arrivals.

text.p: Cotton prices were dragged down on Thursday by rising new crop arrivals and sluggish mill demand, traders said.
Daily new crop arrivals in the Punjab region in north India have risen to 7,000-8,000 bales (170 kg each), they said.

The weak sentiment in the spot section also affected forward delivery contracts, the traders said. Bengal-deshi ready delivery fell 10 rupees to 830/850 per maund (37.32 kg) while November delivery also lost 10 rupees to 870/890 per maund.
In the spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) fell to 12,800/12,900 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 13,200/13,400.
